BOSTON – August 13, 2026 – Realtime Robotics, the leader in industrial AI for automated robot system design and deployment, today announced that Kevin Carlin has been appointed Chief Executive Officer, effective immediately.
BOSTON – August 13, 2026 – Realtime Robotics, the leader in industrial AI for automated robot system design and deployment, today announced that Kevin Carlin has been appointed Chief Executive Officer, effective immediately.
Carlin brings more than two decades of international leadership in semiconductors, industrial automation, and AI to the role. He joined Realtime Robotics in 2022 as Chief Commercial Officer and was promoted to President and Chief Commercial Officer in 2025. Prior to Realtime Robotics, Carlin spent more than 13 years at Analog Devices, where he most recently built an internal startup focused on AI- and machine learning-driven sensing and analytics.
Realtime Robotics’ Resolver platform automates and optimizes the most complex aspects of factory planning and robot system design and deployment.

# Realtime Robotics Signals New Growth Era with CEO Leadership Change  
**BOSTON, MA – August 13, 2026** – In a move that signals a strategic shift from foundational technology development to aggressive market scaling, Realtime Robotics has appointed Kevin Carlin as its new Chief Executive Officer. The appointment comes as the industrial AI specialist sees its core technology, the Resolver platform, gain significant traction among the world's most demanding manufacturers. Carlin succeeds co-founder Peter Howard, who has guided the company from its inception and now transitions to the role of non-executive Chairman of the Board, ensuring his strategic oversight continues as the company enters its next chapter.  
This leadership transition is not merely a change in the C-suite; it is a carefully orchestrated maneuver reflecting a critical inflection point for both Realtime Robotics and the broader industrial automation sector. The company, having proven the value of its technology in the high-stakes automotive world, is now positioning itself to capitalize on that success and scale its impact across global manufacturing.
## Deconstructing the Resolver Revolution  
To understand the significance of Realtime Robotics' growth, one must look beyond the boardroom and onto the factory floor, where the company's Resolver platform is fundamentally altering the economics of automation. For decades, programming multiple industrial robots to work together in a confined space has been a painstaking, manual process. Engineers would spend thousands of hours programming and de-bugging collision avoidance, creating rigid, inflexible production lines.  
Resolver automates this complexity. The AI-powered platform functions like a digital motor cortex for the factory, generating optimized, collision-free motion plans for multiple robots in microseconds. By offloading this planning to the cloud, it allows engineers to design, simulate, and deploy complex robotic workcells with unprecedented speed and flexibility. The result is a dramatic reduction in engineering bottlenecks and program launch times.
